newsitem.title: ITALY: Employers see no end to Italy metalworkers dispute.
newsitem.headline: Employers see no end to Italy metalworkers dispute.

text.p: There is no end in sight to the long-running dispute in the Italian metalworkers and engineering sector, the head of employers' federation Federmeccanica said on Wednesday after meeting Labour Minister Tiziano Treu.
"There is little hope," Michele Figurati told reporters, adding that he was prepared to carry on negotiations.
"This was a private meeting. We're waiting for an (official) call-up," Figurati said of his encounter with Treu, who is trying to broker a deal in the six-month dispute.
In a bid to break the stalemate the government proposed last month that workers should be given a 200,000 lire a month pay rise to cover the 1996-98 contract period.
Figurati said on Wednesday such an offer was "not compatible with costs".

Trade unions, which have accepted the government proposal, announced on Tuesday fresh strike action to put pressure on employers. The decision to hold 10 hours of strikes is due to be formally approved later on Wednesday.
Metalworkers and engineering unions have already staged two-one day stoppages to press their claims.
The employers' federation has refused workers a rise of more than 139,000 lire a month. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
